title: Saved-copy shift search with a heralded filter (T2): tolerance 1 - 1/((16*10^126-1)(625*10^126-1))

claims.statement: For every integer N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, let n = ceil(log2 N), L = 2^n, and k = n+24. The streamed saved-copy shift-search algorithm of proof.md acquires exactly k well-formed DCP copies once through the heralded filter FILTER of proof.md Section 8 (exactly k ideal copies in the clean problem); for n >= 2 it performs r = isqrt(9L) // 4 iterations of its implemented candidate-controlled all-pass reflection and diffusion; for n = 1 (N = 2) it tests t = 0 on all k copies and outputs 0 if all pass and 1 otherwise. The total sequential work in the challenge model is T(N,s) = O(2^(n/2) n^2 log2 n) for n >= 2. A bound valid for all n >= 1 is C 2^(n/2) n^2 max{1,log2 n}, with an absolute C; the n=1 branch has constant work. The eventually positive uniform time envelope B_T(n) = 2^(n/2) n^2 log2 n has exact growth index 1. Work includes initialization, source acquisition, all gates, exact gate decomposition, uniform streamed circuit generation, bit operations, addressing, preprocessing, measurements and output. All constants are absolute and independent of N, s and outcomes. This is a worst-case bound on every execution branch, in the clean problem and under the heralded malformed-copy model of claim 4 (proof.md Section 8), jointly with the other three resource bounds and unconditional recovery of the entire s with probability at least 25573/36864 > 2/3.

For every N >= 2 and every s, if at most floor(epsilon(n) Q) of the Q acquired copies are malformed on every branch, the algorithm recovers the entire s with unconditional probability at least 25573/36864 > 2/3 jointly with the four resource bounds of claims 0-3 in the form stated there (proof.md Lemmas 8.1-8.2). In the clean problem the algorithm is unchanged. No tolerance of undetectable corruption is claimed.

structured.error_model: Heralded malformed-copy model with fraction epsilon(n). Parameters: N >= 2 is the modulus, s in Z/NZ the secret, n = ceil(log2 N), Q the total number of source copies the algorithm acquires on an execution branch, and epsilon(n) the tolerated malformed fraction. Each acquired copy consists of an (n+1)-qubit register of the ideal copy's shape together with one classical herald bit f delivered with it. Copies are delivered one at a time in acquisition order j = 1, ..., Q. Before copy j is delivered, an adversary that knows N, s, the full description of the algorithm and every measurement outcome the algorithm obtained before copy j is delivered, and that may hold, process and measure an arbitrary private quantum system, decides adaptively whether copy j is malformed. A well-formed copy has f = 0 and its register is a fresh copy of rho_s, in tensor product with every other system (earlier copies, the adversary's system and the algorithm's registers). A malformed copy has f = 1 and its register is in an arbitrary state chosen by the adversary, possibly entangled with the adversary's private system and with other malformed copies. On every execution branch at most floor(epsilon(n) Q) of the Q acquired copies are malformed. The herald is always correct, so malformation is detectable (an erasure-type error); its timing, its number within the promise and the malformed register contents are adversarial. In the clean problem no herald is supplied and every copy is well-formed. No source control, purification access or preparation inverse is supplied.
